title: Quantitative Analysis of Defective Graphene Induced by Electron Irradiation via Persistent Homology
content: Atomic control of defect structures in graphene has been of interest because the defects in graphene alter its electrical, thermal, and magnetic properties [1-3]. It is well known that electron beam irradiation above its knock-on damage threshold ∼86 keV induces defects in graphene. In order to control the defect structures by changing the total dose, dose rate, and energy of electron beam, we need to establish quantitative relationship between the defect structures and electron beam parameters. Furthermore, more specifically, descriptors that quantitatively describe the defect structures are necessary. So far, however, the structural descriptors extracted from TEM images of defective graphene have been limited to average structural information such as crystallinity, defined as the percentage of hexagons in all polygons, and distribution of bond lengths and bond angles [4, 5]. In addition to those descriptors, extracting information about local structure and global connectivity is important for more precise structural control.
